rows.question: When does my maternity leave start if my due date is 15 November 2026?
rows.reply:
Under the Mutterschutz (statutory maternity protection period) rules, the period before the birth covers the last six weeks before the delivery. The law says the employer may not employ a pregnant woman "in den letzten sechs Wochen vor der Entbindung" (in the last six weeks before the delivery), unless she expressly declares that she is willing to work. She can withdraw that declaration at any time for the future.

The six weeks are counted back from the expected delivery date. The law names the source of that date: "der voraussichtliche Tag der Entbindung … wie er sich aus dem ärztlichen Zeugnis oder dem Zeugnis einer Hebamme oder eines Entbindungspflegers ergibt". This means the expected date stated in a certificate from a doctor, midwife or male midwife. If that certificate gives 15 November 2026, the period before the birth is the six weeks leading up to that date. The excerpts do not set out how the individual days are counted, so they do not fix the exact first day.

If the baby is not born on the expected day, the period before the birth becomes shorter or longer to match.

After the birth, the employer may not employ the mother until eight weeks have passed. This rises to twelve weeks:
1. for premature births,
2. for multiple births, and
3. where a doctor confirms within the first eight weeks that the child has a disability. This extension applies only if the mother applies for it.

If the baby comes early, the period after the birth is extended by the time that was lost before the birth.

The official family portal states that self-employed women are not covered by the Mutterschutz law.

Whether and how these rules apply to your own employment is not something this answer can decide. Your employer and your health insurance fund (Krankenkasse) are the places to confirm your dates.

rows.question: How long after birth can we apply for Elterngeld without losing money?
rows.reply:
There is no fixed application deadline in the excerpts, but applying late costs money. The law limits how far back Elterngeld (parental allowance) is paid. It is paid retroactively only for the last three months of the child's life before the month of life in which the application was received: "Es wird rückwirkend nur für die letzten drei Lebensmonate vor Beginn des Lebensmonats geleistet, in dem der Antrag auf Elterngeld eingegangen ist." Months of the child's life earlier than those three are not paid.

Elterngeld can be drawn from the day of birth ("Es kann ab dem Tag der Geburt bezogen werden"), and it is paid in monthly amounts for the child's months of life. So an application received within the first months of the child's life keeps those first months inside the period that can still be paid. Applications received later lose whole months of payment.

The application must be made in writing ("Elterngeld ist schriftlich zu beantragen").

Whether and how much you receive is decided by your Elterngeldstelle, not here.

rows.question: How much notice do I have to give my employer for Elternzeit?
rows.reply:
Under federal law, the notice period for Elternzeit (parental leave (unpaid job-protected leave)) depends on when the leave falls. You must request it from your employer in text form, BEEG §16(1):

- For leave before your child's third birthday: at least seven weeks before the leave begins ("spätestens sieben Wochen").
- For leave between the third birthday and the end of the child's eighth year: at least 13 weeks before the leave begins ("spätestens 13 Wochen").

When you request leave for the period before the third birthday, you must also state at the same time which periods within two years you will take as Elternzeit ("für welche Zeiten innerhalb von zwei Jahren").

The Familienportal explains that text form means you can give notice by email or by a letter without a signature.

Exceptions in the statute:

- **Urgent reasons:** a reasonable shorter period is possible as an exception ("Bei dringenden Gründen ist ausnahmsweise eine angemessene kürzere Frist möglich").
- **Leave directly after maternity protection:** if a mother cannot make the request in time for leave that follows straight on from the maternity protection period, for a reason that is not her fault, she can make up the request within one week after that reason ends. This is BEEG §16(2).

Your employer is required to certify your Elternzeit, BEEG §16(1).

For children born before 1 July 2015, the Familienportal describes a different rule. The transitional provision that governs those births is not among the excerpts here, so it is not stated here.

rows.question: How long is maternity protection after the birth if the baby comes early?
rows.reply:
Under the Mutterschutz (statutory maternity protection period) rules, your employer may not employ you until eight weeks after the birth (MuSchG §3(2)). If the baby comes early, the answer depends on whether the birth counts as a premature birth ("Frühgeburt").

Born before the due date, but not a premature birth: the period before the birth is counted from the expected due date. If the birth happens on a different day, that pre-birth period is shortened accordingly (MuSchG §3(1)). The days lost before the birth are added after it: "Bei vorzeitiger Entbindung verlängert sich die Schutzfrist nach der Entbindung ... um den Zeitraum der Verkürzung der Schutzfrist vor der Entbindung" (MuSchG §3(2)). So the period after the birth is eight weeks plus the number of days the baby arrived early. The official family portal describes the total as still 14 weeks.

Premature birth: the period after the birth is extended to twelve weeks ("verlängert sich auf zwölf Wochen ... bei Frühgeburten", MuSchG §3(2)). The days lost before the birth are added on top of the twelve weeks as well, under the same sentence of §3(2). The family portal gives a birth weight under 2,500 grams as one example of a premature birth. It describes the total period as rising from 14 to 18 weeks.

The statute gives three grounds for the twelve-week period after the birth:
1. premature births;
2. multiple births (twins, triplets or more);
3. a disability of the child, within the meaning of § 2(1) sentence 1 of Book IX of the Social Code, that a doctor confirms before eight weeks after the birth. This third ground extends the period only if the woman applies for it.

The twelve-week extension does not apply in the case of a stillbirth (MuSchG §3(2)).

rows.question: Can my employer dismiss me while I am pregnant?
rows.reply:
As a rule, no. Kündigungsschutz (protection against dismissal) for pregnant women is set out in MuSchG §17. Dismissal of a woman is not permitted ("unzulässig"):
1. during her pregnancy,
2. until four months after a miscarriage after the twelfth week of pregnancy, and
3. until the end of her protection period after the birth, and at least until four months after the birth.

This protection applies if the employer knows about the pregnancy, miscarriage or birth when dismissing her, or is told within two weeks after the dismissal is received ("innerhalb von zwei Wochen nach Zugang der Kündigung"). Missing the two weeks does no harm if it was not the woman's fault and she informs the employer without delay ("unverzüglich"). The protection also applies if she did not yet know she was pregnant, but she must already have been pregnant when she received the dismissal.

There are exceptions. In special cases not connected with the pregnancy, a miscarriage or the birth, the supreme authority of the Land responsible for occupational safety, or a body it designates, may exceptionally declare a dismissal permissible. Such a dismissal must be in writing and state the reason. The Familienportal gives examples: the company is insolvent, the business is partly closed, a small business cannot continue without a qualified replacement, or a particularly serious breach of duty. Without the authority's approval, the dismissal is invalid ("unwirksam").

If you are dismissed without that approval, the Familienportal says you must bring a claim before the competent labour court (Arbeitsgericht), "normalerweise innerhalb von 3 Wochen" (normally within 3 weeks) of receiving the written dismissal. If no claim is brought, the dismissal is treated as effective. You can bring the claim yourself or through a lawyer, and you can also make it orally at the court office. The Familienportal also says you should involve the competent supervisory authority. This authority is responsible for compliance with the maternity protection law, and you can contact it with questions.

If you take parental leave after the birth, the special protection can be extended.

Whether a particular dismissal is permissible is decided by the supervisory authority for maternity protection in your Land, and its validity by the labour court.

rows.question: Is there an income limit above which we get no Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes. Under the statute, the claim to Elterngeld (parental allowance) lapses above a set zu versteuerndes Einkommen (taxable income).

The rule in BEEG §1(8):
- A single entitled person loses the claim if their taxable income in the last completed tax assessment period before the birth was more than 175,000 euros ("in Höhe von mehr als 175 000 Euro").
- Where another person also meets the conditions (for example, the other parent living in the same household with the child), the claim lapses if the two people's taxable incomes added together are more than 175,000 euros ("wenn die Summe des zu versteuernden Einkommens beider Personen mehr als 175 000 Euro beträgt").

The limit is about taxable income, not gross pay. The official family portal notes that gross income is usually considerably higher than taxable income, because deductions are subtracted to reach it. The taxable figure appears in your Steuerbescheid (tax assessment notice) from the Finanzamt.

If the tax assessment for that period is not yet available when you apply, and it cannot yet be said whether the limit is exceeded, BEEG §8(3) says the decision on Elterngeld is made provisionally until the required information is provided.

The official family portal says that different limits applied to births before 1 April 2025. The excerpts do not include the statute's transitional provision, so I cannot tell you which limit governs a particular birth date.

The Elterngeldstelle responsible for your district decides whether the limit applies in your case. This is federal law and applies everywhere in Germany, including Hessen.

rows.question: How many months of Elterngeld can we get in total?
rows.reply:
Elterngeld (parental allowance) is paid in monthly amounts for the child's months of life, not calendar months. The number of months depends on which version is drawn and which conditions are met. BEEG §4 sets these limits.

Basic Elterngeld:
- Parents together are entitled to 12 monthly amounts: "Die Eltern haben gemeinsam Anspruch auf zwölf Monatsbeträge Basiselterngeld."
- They are jointly entitled to two further months ("Partnermonate") if one parent's earned income is reduced in two months of the child's life.
- One parent can receive at most 12 monthly amounts of basic Elterngeld. On top of that, a parent can receive at most four monthly amounts of the partnership bonus ("Partnerschaftsbonus") under §4b.
- A parent is only entitled to Elterngeld if they receive it for at least two months of the child's life.
- Basic Elterngeld can be drawn until the child completes the 14th month of life.

Elterngeld Plus:
- Instead of one month of basic Elterngeld, a parent can receive two months of Elterngeld Plus.
- Elterngeld Plus can be drawn until the child completes the 32nd month of life. This applies only while, from the 15th month, at least one parent draws it in consecutive months.

Partnership bonus:
- Its conditions are set in §4b, which is not among the excerpts.
- The federal family portal describes it like this: each parent can get up to 4 additional months of Elterngeld Plus if both parents work part-time at the same time.

Premature births (§4(5)):
If the child was born early, the joint entitlement to basic Elterngeld is higher. The amount depends on how early the birth was:
- at least 6 weeks before the expected delivery date: 13 monthly amounts
- at least 8 weeks early: 14 monthly amounts
- at least 12 weeks early: 15 monthly amounts
- at least 16 weeks early: 16 monthly amounts

The expected delivery date is the one shown in the doctor's or midwife's certificate. In these cases the maximum per parent rises to 13, 14, 15 or 16 monthly amounts of basic Elterngeld respectively, plus up to four months of partnership bonus. The time window for basic Elterngeld extends to the 15th, 16th, 17th or 18th month of life respectively.

Adopted children:
For adopted children, Elterngeld can be drawn from the date the child joins the household, at the latest until the child's eighth birthday.

In the application, you state which months you claim for basic Elterngeld, Elterngeld Plus or the partnership bonus (BEEG §7(1)).

How many months your family receives depends on which of these conditions apply to you. That is decided by the Elterngeld office responsible for your district, not here. You submit your application there.

rows.question: What is the Partnerschaftsbonus and who qualifies?
rows.reply:
The Partnerschaftsbonus (partnership bonus months) is an extra payment for parents who both work part-time at the same time. Under BEEG §4b(1), each parent receives "einen zusätzlichen Monatsbetrag Elterngeld Plus" (an additional monthly amount of the ElterngeldPlus form of parental allowance) for each month of the child's life in which the conditions are met.

Conditions for couples (BEEG §4b):
- Both parents work "nicht weniger als 24 und nicht mehr als 32 Wochenstunden im Durchschnitt des Lebensmonats": at least 24 and at most 32 hours a week, averaged over the child's month of life.
- Both parents meet the general conditions of BEEG §1. The excerpts do not set out what §1 requires.
- Each parent can receive at most four monthly amounts. The bonus can only be drawn if it is taken for at least two months of the child's life.
- Both parents must draw it at the same time, in consecutive months of the child's life ("nur gleichzeitig und in aufeinander folgenden Lebensmonaten").
- If it later turns out that the conditions were not met in every month applied for, the requirement of consecutive months still counts as met (§4b(5)).

The four bonus months come on top of the maximum of twelve months of basic parental allowance per parent (BEEG §4(4)).

One parent alone (BEEG §4c(2)): a single parent can receive these additional monthly amounts. That parent must work 24 to 32 hours a week on average in at least two and at most four consecutive months of the child's life. This applies where one of the following three grounds in §4c(1) exists:
1. the parent meets the conditions for the tax relief for single parents under §24b(1) and (3) of the Income Tax Act, and the other parent lives neither with them nor with the child;
2. care by the other parent would endanger the child's welfare within the meaning of §1666(1) and (2) of the Civil Code;
3. care by the other parent is impossible, in particular because of serious illness or severe disability. Economic reasons and being busy with other activities do not count.

If one of these grounds arises while the parents are already drawing the bonus, one parent can continue drawing it alone (§4b(4)).

The federal guidance page states that the bonus is calculated the same way as ElterngeldPlus and amounts to between 150 and 900 euros per parent per month, depending on income before the birth. It also says separated parents can receive it. The guidance explains the rules for children born after August 2021. For children born before 1 September 2021, it says partly different rules apply.

Whether a particular family qualifies, and for how much, is decided only by the responsible Elterngeldstelle (parental allowance office) for your district, not by this service.

rows.question: We forgot to apply for Kindergeld. How far back will they pay?
rows.reply:
Kindergeld (child benefit) is paid back for at most six months. The law says that payment of Kindergeld is made retroactively only for the last six months before the start of the month in which the application is received: "rückwirkend nur für die letzten sechs Monate vor Beginn des Monats, in dem der Antrag auf Kindergeld eingegangen ist" (EStG §70(1)).

This is a limit on payment, not an application deadline. Months earlier than those six are not paid. The same provision says that the entitlement itself is not affected by this payment limit: "Der Anspruch auf Kindergeld nach § 62 bleibt von dieser Auszahlungsbeschränkung unberührt." Because the six months are counted back from the month the application arrives, each further month without an application means one more earlier month that is not paid.

The Familienportal says that back payment applies where Kindergeld was due but not paid, for example because no application was made. When applying retroactively, it says you should state in the application that you are applying retroactively and from when you want to receive Kindergeld.

Kindergeld must be applied for in writing (BKGG §9(1)). The application should be made to the responsible Familienkasse (BKGG §9(1)), which the Familienportal describes as the Familienkasse of your Agentur für Arbeit. The Familienkasse decides your individual case, including which months are paid.

rows.question: How much Kindergeld do we get per month for our first child?
rows.reply:
The law sets the monthly amount of Kindergeld (child benefit) at 259 euros for each child: "Das Kindergeld beträgt monatlich für jedes Kind 259 Euro." The same figure applies to every child, including a first child. It is stated identically in the Income Tax Act and the Federal Child Benefit Act.

Kindergeld is paid monthly from the start of the month in which the conditions are met until the end of the month in which they cease to be met. For example, a child born on 25 May brings full Kindergeld for May.

The law also says the amount is raised when the tax allowances for children are raised. So the figure can change over time.

Whether your family is entitled is not something this answer can decide. That decision is made by the responsible office when it handles your application. Kindergeld applications can be made online with the Bundesagentur für Arbeit.

rows.question: How quickly do we have to register the birth at the Standesamt?
rows.reply:
The birth must be reported to the Standesamt (civil registry office) responsible for the place where the child was born, within one week. The statute says the birth is to be reported "binnen einer Woche" (within one week) to the Standesamt "in dessen Zuständigkeitsbereich es geboren ist" (in whose area the child was born).

The law allows the report to be made orally or in writing by the persons it names, or in writing by the institutions it names. If your child was born in a hospital, birth centre or maternity clinic, the official family portal says the institution notifies the responsible Standesamt and sends it the birth certificate issued at the birth. If your child was born at home, the midwife or doctor issues that certificate, and you must present it to the responsible Standesamt within one week.

For a stillbirth, the statute sets a shorter period: the report must be made "spätestens am dritten auf die Geburt folgenden Werktag" (at the latest on the third working day after the birth).

The Standesamt in the place of birth is the authority for registering the birth. For which documents your Standesamt asks for, check that Standesamt's own website.

rows.question: What do we need to bring to the Standesamt to register the birth?
rows.reply:
The rule on documents is set by federal regulation (PStV §33). When a birth is registered, the Standesamt (civil registry office) is to ask for the following:

1. If the parents are married to each other: their marriage certificate or a certified extract from the marriage register, and their own birth certificates if the parents' birth registration details do not appear on the marriage certificate. The marriage certificate is required even if the marriage has been dissolved.
2. If the parents are not married to each other: the mother's birth certificate. If paternity has already been acknowledged, also the acknowledgement declarations and the father's birth certificate, and any joint custody declarations.
3. An identity card, passport or other recognised passport substitute for the parents.
4. If the birth is reported in person: a certificate of the birth issued by the doctor or midwife who was present at the birth.

The Standesamt may also ask for further documents where they are needed to prove the details given.

If your child was born in a hospital, birth centre or maternity clinic, the facility notifies the responsible Standesamt and sends it the birth certificate itself. If your child was born at home, the midwife or doctor issues it and you present it to the Standesamt. The responsible Standesamt is the one for the place where the child was born.

If the parents are foreign nationals, the Standesamt will also ask whether a parent holds an unlimited right of residence, or a residence permit under the EU–Switzerland free movement agreement. This is used to check whether the child acquired German citizenship at birth under StAG §4(3).

The federal portal says the Standesamt's own website lists any further documents it requires. Check the website of the Standesamt for the place of birth.

rows.question: Does my Krankenkasse pay for a midwife?
rows.reply:
Yes, the law gives this entitlement to women insured with a Krankenkasse (statutory health insurer). Under SGB V §24d, the insured woman is entitled to midwife help during pregnancy, at the birth and after the birth ("während der Schwangerschaft, bei und nach der Entbindung Anspruch auf ärztliche Betreuung sowie auf Hebammenhilfe"). This includes the examinations to confirm the pregnancy and the prenatal check-ups.

After the birth, the entitlement to care from a Hebamme (midwife) during the postpartum period runs until twelve weeks after the birth ("bis zum Ablauf von zwölf Wochen nach der Geburt"). Anything beyond that needs a doctor's order ("weitergehende Leistungen bedürfen der ärztlichen Anordnung").

If the mother cannot care for the baby after the birth, the insured child has its own entitlement to the midwife services that relate to the child.

The Familienportal also says that every woman with statutory health insurance is entitled to support from a Hebamme. If you are privately insured, private insurance is outside what this product covers. The Familienportal advises checking with your private insurer beforehand which services it pays for.

This is the general rule. Whether a particular service is covered in your case is decided by your Krankenkasse.

rows.question: When are the first check-ups for the baby?
rows.reply:
The first Vorsorgeuntersuchung (routine preventive check-up) checks are set out in the federal children's directive (Kinder-Richtlinie). It lists ten check-ups in the first six years of life, named U1 to U9 (including U7a). Each must take place within a set period, with a tolerance window. The first ones are:

- U1: immediately after the birth ("Unmittelbar nach der Geburt"). It should be done within the first 30 minutes after the birth ("innerhalb der ersten 30 Minuten nach der Geburt"). If no doctor is present at the birth but a midwife is, the midwife should carry it out.
- U2: 3rd to 10th day of life ("3.-10. Lebenstag"). The tolerance window is the 3rd to 14th day ("3.-14. Lebenstag").
- U3: 4th to 5th week of life ("4.-5. Lebenswoche"). The tolerance window is the 3rd to 8th week ("3.-8. Lebenswoche").
- U4: 3rd to 4th month of life ("3.-4. Lebensmonat"). The tolerance window is the 2nd to 4½th month ("2.-4 ½ Lebensmonat").
- U5: 6th to 7th month of life ("6.-7. Lebensmonat"). The tolerance window is the 5th to 8th month ("5.-8. Lebensmonat").

The directive says the check-ups can only be used within these periods and tolerance windows ("können nur in den jeweils angegebenen Zeiträumen unter Berücksichtigung folgender Toleranzgrenzen in Anspruch genommen werden").

If your baby was born early, the same periods still apply ("Auch bei Frühgeborenen sind die Untersuchungszeiträume einzuhalten"). Being born early is taken into account when the results are assessed.

Children are entitled to these early-detection check-ups until their 18th birthday.

rows.question: What is Mutterschaftsgeld and when do I apply for it?
rows.reply:
Mutterschaftsgeld (maternity pay from the health insurer) is a payment for the protection periods before and after the birth, and for the day of the birth itself. MuSchG §19 says it is paid "für die Zeit der Schutzfristen vor und nach der Entbindung sowie für den Entbindungstag".

Who pays depends on how you are insured:

- If you are a member of a statutory health insurance fund, you receive it under the rules of the Social Code, Book V (MuSchG §19(1)). Under SGB V §24i(2), for women in employment it is based on average net daily pay over the last three settled calendar months before the protection period, and is at most 13 euros per calendar day ("höchstens 13 Euro für den Kalendertag").
- If you are employed, your employer pays a top-up ("Zuschuss zum Mutterschaftsgeld"). This is the difference between 13 euros and your average net daily pay over the last three settled calendar months before the protection period (MuSchG §20(1)).
- If you are not a member of a statutory health insurance fund, Mutterschaftsgeld is paid from federal funds, "insgesamt höchstens 210 Euro" (at most 210 euros in total). It is paid "auf Antrag vom Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung", meaning on application to the Federal Office for Social Security (MuSchG §19(2)).

When it is paid: according to the Familienportal, the protection periods normally begin 6 weeks before the calculated due date and end 8 weeks after the birth. For payment before the birth, the decisive document is a certificate from a doctor or midwife stating the expected date of delivery (SGB V §24i(3)).

When to apply: the excerpts do not set out an application date, a deadline or an application procedure. For statutory members, ask your statutory health insurance fund. If you are not in statutory health insurance, the application goes to the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung. Whether you qualify, and how much you receive, is decided by the paying body, not by this service.

rows.question: We are not married. Is my partner automatically the legal father?
rows.reply:
No. Under German law, being the mother's partner does not by itself make him the legal father. The law (BGB §1592) names three ways a man becomes the father of a child: he "zum Zeitpunkt der Geburt mit der Mutter des Kindes verheiratet ist" (is married to the mother at the time of the birth), he "die Vaterschaft anerkannt hat" (has acknowledged paternity), or his paternity has been established by a court.

If you are not married at the time of the birth, he must make a Vaterschaftsanerkennung (acknowledgement of paternity) to count legally as the father. The acknowledgement is voluntary and needs the mother's consent.

The acknowledgement can be made before the child is born: "Die Anerkennung ist schon vor der Geburt des Kindes zulässig" (BGB §1594(4)). It is not effective while another man's paternity exists (BGB §1594(2)). An acknowledgement made subject to a condition or a time limit is invalid (BGB §1594(3)).

The father must make his declaration in person at a responsible office, for example the youth welfare office, a registry office, a local court or a notary. The mother must also declare her consent in person. The office records both declarations. Depending on the Bundesland, an acknowledgement at a notary or local court can cost a fee.

If the father does not want to acknowledge paternity, or the mother does not consent, the child, the mother or the presumed biological father can apply to a court to have paternity established.

Acknowledging paternity does not automatically give him parental custody. If you are not married at the birth, the mother has custody from the birth. For joint custody, both parents must also declare that they want to share custody, or a court must decide this. Marrying after the birth also creates joint custody. Your local youth welfare office advises on questions about custody.

rows.question: How do unmarried parents get joint custody?
rows.reply:
If the parents are not married to each other when the child is born, the mother has parental custody alone unless one of the routes below applies (BGB §1626a(3)).

The law gives unmarried parents three ways to joint custody (BGB §1626a(1)):
1. Both parents declare that they want to take on custody together. Each declaration is a Sorgeerklärung (declaration of joint custody).
2. The parents marry each other.
3. The family court transfers custody to both parents jointly.

The father must first be legally recognised as the father. According to the federal family portal, this happens when he acknowledges the child as his own with the mother's consent, or when a court establishes paternity. Acknowledging paternity does not by itself give him custody. A Sorgeerklärung or a court decision is still needed.

The family court acts on the application of one parent. It transfers custody, or part of it, to both parents jointly "wenn die Übertragung dem Kindeswohl nicht widerspricht" (if the transfer does not conflict with the child's welfare). If the other parent gives no reasons against joint custody, and none are otherwise apparent, the law presumes that joint custody does not conflict with the child's welfare (BGB §1626a(2)). The family portal adds that in this situation the court decides in a simplified procedure. The youth welfare office is not heard, and the parents are not heard in person.

When a Sorgeerklärung is made, or a final court decision transfers joint custody, an entry is made in the custody register kept by the responsible youth welfare office (SGB VIII §58(1)).

The excerpts do not say where or in what form a Sorgeerklärung is made. Unmarried mothers and fathers have a legal right to advice from the youth welfare office. This covers making a Sorgeerklärung and the option of a court transfer of joint custody (SGB VIII §18(2)). Your local youth welfare office is the place to ask about the procedure. The family court decides applications for a court transfer.

rows.question: Where do we apply for Elterngeld in Frankfurt?

The responsible one is the office for the district where the child has their residence in Germany ("inländischen Wohnsitz") when the first application is made.

The federal family portal says you can apply at an Elterngeldstelle in person or digitally, and that all states offer a digital application. It tells you to contact the Elterngeldstelle responsible for your child's place of residence. The application must be made in writing ("schriftlich zu beantragen").

It also lists the body that supervises Elterngeld at the Regierungspräsidium Gießen. Use that page to find the office covering Frankfurt. Payment is made backdated for at most the three months before the month your application arrives. Earlier months are not paid.

rows.question: Will our baby automatically be German if we are both Indian citizens?
rows.reply:
Not by descent. Under StAG §4(1), a child acquires German Staatsangehörigkeit (citizenship) by birth if a parent holds German Staatsangehörigkeit.

For children of foreign parents, StAG §4(3) sets a separate rule. A child born in Germany ("Durch die Geburt im Inland") acquires German Staatsangehörigkeit if one parent meets both of these conditions:
1. has had lawful habitual residence in Germany for five years ("seit fünf Jahren rechtmäßig seinen gewöhnlichen Aufenthalt im Inland"), and
2. holds a permanent right of residence ("ein unbefristetes Aufenthaltsrecht"), or, as a Swiss citizen or a Swiss citizen's family member, a residence permit under the 1999 EU–Switzerland free movement agreement.

When the child acquires citizenship this way, it is entered in the birth register where the birth is recorded.

How this is checked: under PStV §34, the civil registry office asks for these details when the birth is reported. If the details indicate that a parent holds such a residence status, the office gets written information from the foreigners' authority. That information confirms whether the details are correct and whether the parent had five years of lawful habitual residence in Germany at the time of the birth. The office must also request this information if you give no details or if it doubts them. The civil registry office then decides whether the child acquired German citizenship and records the result.

Whether your child meets these conditions is decided by the civil registry office where the birth is registered. This service cannot assess your case.

If the child does not acquire German citizenship, AufenthG §33 sets three rules for a child born in Germany:
- If both parents hold an Aufenthaltserlaubnis, a Niederlassungserlaubnis or an Erlaubnis zum Daueraufenthalt – EU at the time of birth, the child is granted a residence permit "von Amts wegen" (without an application). The same applies if the parent with sole custody holds one of them.
- If only one parent holds one of these, the child may be granted one.
- If a parent holds a visa or may stay without a visa, the child's stay counts as permitted until that visa or visa-free stay ends.

The excerpts do not cover your child's Indian citizenship. Ask the Indian consular authorities about that.

rows.question: We are getting Mutterschaftsgeld. Does that reduce our Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes, the law credits Mutterschaftsgeld (maternity pay from the health insurer) against Elterngeld (parental allowance). Whether and by how much your own Elterngeld changes is decided by the Elterngeldstelle for your district, not here.

What the law says:

- BEEG §3(1) lists the income that is credited ("angerechnet") against Elterngeld. This includes Mutterschaftsgeld under the statutory health insurance rules and the employer's top-up to Mutterschaftsgeld under MuSchG §20. Both count only where they are due "für die Zeit ab dem Tag der Geburt des Kindes", from the day of birth onwards.
- There is one exception. The one-off Mutterschaftsgeld under MuSchG §19(2) is not credited. This is the payment for women who are not members of a statutory health insurer, "insgesamt höchstens 210 Euro", paid by the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung.
- Elterngeld normally keeps 300 euros free of crediting. BEEG §3(2) says this does not apply where income under Nummer 1 to 3, which includes Mutterschaftsgeld, is credited.
- If the maternity payments are due for only part of a month of the child's life, they are credited only against the matching part of Elterngeld (BEEG §3(1)). The Familienportal explains that the crediting is done to the day.

What this means in practice, according to the Familienportal:

- If the maternity payments are higher than Elterngeld, only the maternity payments are paid.
- If Elterngeld is higher, the difference is paid as Elterngeld on top.
- Months in which maternity payments are received for the same child "gelten bei Ihnen als Monate mit Basiselterngeld" (count as months of basic Elterngeld). This is so even if they are due for only one day in that month.
- The maternity payments are credited only against the mother's Elterngeld, not the father's ("nur auf das Elterngeld der Mutter").

How this applies to your family, and the amount you would receive, is decided by the Elterngeldstelle for your district. In Hessen, that is the Elterngeldstelle responsible where you live.

rows.question: Can I work while receiving Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes. Working does not by itself rule out Elterngeld (parental allowance), but the law limits how much you may work.

One of the conditions for Elterngeld is that the person does "keine oder keine volle Erwerbstätigkeit" (no work, or no full-time work). The law says a person is not in full-time work if any one of these applies:
1. their working time does not exceed "32 Wochenstunden im Durchschnitt des Lebensmonats" (32 hours a week on average over the child's month of life);
2. they are in employment for vocational training ("Beschäftigung zur Berufsbildung"); or
3. they work as a suitable childminder ("Kindertagespflegeperson") within the meaning of §§ 23 and 43 SGB VIII.
The law also treats people who are temporarily not working as employed while they are in an employment relationship or self-employed.

Working affects the amount. The maximum of 1,800 euros a month applies to full months in which the person has no income from work. For months after the birth with income from work that is on average lower than before the birth, Elterngeld is paid as a percentage of the difference between the two incomes. For this, pre-birth income is counted at no more than 2,770 euros. Elterngeld is paid at least at 300 euros.

Instead of one month of the basic amount, a person can take two months of the Plus variant.

If the application states that you expect income from work during the payment period, the amount is decided provisionally. After the payment period ends, you must prove your actual income from work for that time. If the application says you expect no income from work, Elterngeld is paid subject to revocation in case you do have such income.

The official guidance page notes that its explanation applies to children born after August 2021, and that partly different rules apply to children born before 1 September 2021. The excerpts do not contain those earlier rules.

Only your Elterngeldstelle decides whether you qualify and how much you receive.
